lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Kenji, this is Luis. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about fruit at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Kind of down this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to walk 10 minutes on 5 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It didn't happen this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just get out there, even when it's hot.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After treatment I had no energy at all. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I just didn't feel like it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walking going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can you do it in the morning instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My diabetes is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to walk 10 minutes on 5 days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 4. Maybe 5.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the rain gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: getting started made this week harder, you still got 0 days in, and your plan is to walk 10 minutes on 5 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Kenji. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Knee pain as reason against walking
Diabetes as personal reason for change

flags.reason: Participant said 'kind of down this week' and coach said 'Okay' and moved on without exploring mood.
'Just get out there, even when it's hot' is unsolicited advice that dismisses the knee and energy barriers.
After 'My diabetes is why I'm doing this,' coach asked about the daughter instead of exploring the health motivation.
'Next week I want you to walk 10 minutes on 5 days' imposes the goal rather than collaborating on it.

score.summary: The coach reviewed the prior goal, built a concrete plan with a rain backup, and summarized well, which gave Kenji a clear next step. However, the coach brushed past his 'kind of down' comment, persuaded twice, and missed his diabetes motivation, reducing the partnership and empathy.
strengths: Line 12: open question 'Why is this important to you right now?' elicited the diabetes motivation.
Line 42: open question about a backup plan for rain led to a concrete plan from Kenji.
Line 44: clear summary confirmed the plan with Kenji.
coaching_tips: Line 6: when Kenji says he is 'kind of down,' pause and explore mood with an open question before moving to goals.
Line 10 and line 38: replace directives ('Just get out there', 'I want you to') with options or ask permission first.
Line 36: after Kenji's diabetes reason at line 35, reflect it back and ask what it means to him before shifting topics.
Line 21 shows good complex reflection; use more of these in place of advice.
